commands: ros2 pkg create --build-type ament_python --node-name patrol patrol --dependencies rclpy geometry_msgs

tests.name: pytest: select_command(pose) returns fixed forward+turn velocity
unremapped patrol publishes to /cmd_vel with 0 subscribers; /turtle1/cmd_vel has 0 publishers
pose unchanged while patrol publishes to the wrong topic
remapped patrol (-r cmd_vel:=/turtle1/cmd_vel) is matched by turtlesim's subscription
measured command rate over 10s is ~10.0 Hz, matching the 0.1s timer
pose changes while remapped patrol runs, confirming delivered motion

defect.reproducer: `ros2 run patrol patrol` without remap publishes Twist to the relative topic `/cmd_vel` (resolved at the node's own namespace), not `/turtle1/cmd_vel`. `ros2 topic info /cmd_vel --verbose` shows Publisher count 1 / Subscription count 0; `ros2 topic info /turtle1/cmd_vel --verbose` at the same time shows Publisher count 0 / Subscription count 1. The turtle's pose does not change (evidence/pr03/demo-run.txt).
defect.root_cause: ROS 2 topic names are resolved relative to a node's namespace unless given as fully-qualified (leading '/') or explicitly remapped; 'cmd_vel' in the publisher code resolves to '/cmd_vel' at the node's top-level namespace, which has no relation to the '/turtle1/cmd_vel' name turtlesim actually subscribes to, even though the message type matches exactly.
defect.proof_after: Running `ros2 run patrol patrol --ros-args -r cmd_vel:=/turtle1/cmd_vel` remaps the relative name to `/turtle1/cmd_vel` at launch time without touching the source code. `ros2 topic info /turtle1/cmd_vel --verbose` now shows both the patrol publisher and the turtlesim subscription on the same topic; `ros2 topic hz /turtle1/cmd_vel` measures 10.000 Hz over a 10s window (matching the 0.1s timer exactly), and the turtle's pose changes accordingly (evidence/pr03/demo-run.txt, demo.md).
